title: VPC post-deploy assertions: liveness, model-load, and smoke orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build an automated, deterministic post-deploy assertions runner for VPC/private deployments that validates API readiness, model load behavior under small-to-medium concurrency, and smoke-level correctness checks before promoting capacity to production.

Scope:
- Orchestrate a three-stage assertion pipeline executed after Terraform apply and service start: 1) API Liveness + auth handshake, 2) Model load & KV-cache priming under staged concurrency, 3) Smoke functional checks (end-to-end requests including streaming and function-call paths).
- Integrate with existing Terraform modules so a `postdeploy_assertions` flag in the module triggers a runbook CI job or on-host agent invocation.
- Emit structured results to Console telemetry (per-check latency, error-class, model-load time, memory pressure), and fail fast with clear remediation hints.

Success criteria:
- Automated run completes within 12 minutes for a standard 4-GPU private deployment and returns a pass/fail status to the deploy pipeline.
- Detects model load regressions: >15% slower load time than baseline marks FAIL.
- API handshake (mTLS/CBOR token) completes within 500ms median.
- Smoke checks must cover generation, streaming, embeddings, and function-like tool call path with no 5xx errors.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Prefer an orchestrator approach (stateless job runner in the control plane) vs. on-instance agent for easier retries; chosen hybrid: orchestrator triggers an agent-runner inside the VPC to avoid exposing credentials, but uses control-plane scheduling metadata.
- To limit cost and false-positive flakiness, we stage concurrency (1 -> 4 -> 12 concurrent simulated clients) with retries and backoff; extremes are left to separate load-tests.
- Use lightweight synthetic prompts that exercise long KV-cache paths to validate attention and caching behavior without incurring heavy token bills.

Implementation plan:
1) IaC: add `postdeploy_assertions` toggle and SSM/remote-exec hook to existing private module in terraform-private-modules repo. (PR link in comments)
2) Orchestrator: small dispatcher service change to schedule assertion job and wait on agent heartbeat with a 20-minute timeout.
3) Agent runner: container image that performs checks, uploads JSON result to S3 and writes status to Console API.
4) Telemetry: add new metrics + traces to Console (assertion.duration, model_load.time, smoke.error_rate) and a dashboard with pass/fail + historical baselines.
5) Alerting: failures during deploy mark the deployment as Blocked and open an incident snooze with remediation hints.

Observability & runbook:
- Attach runbook with common failure signatures (K8s OOM on model-load, KMS auth failures, kernel missing, network egress blocked).
- Provide direct links in failure message to contributor logs, instance syslogs, and the most recent successful run baseline.

Risks:
- Potential for flaky failures due to transient infra (we mitigate with cooldown and 2 retries).
- Model onboarding differences across architectures may require per-model thresholds; plan to seed a small matrix and iterate.

Deliverables:
- Terraform change + example invocation (private-module v1.8).
- Orchestrator patch + agent runner container image.
- Console telemetry & dashboard.
- Runbook doc and PRD link.

2026-03-11 - Leah Ortiz (PM Review): Reviewed success criteria. Requested adding explicit pass thresholds for API handshake and to include function-call path in smoke checks. Marked as high priority for next release train.

2026-03-12 - SRE Feedback (Simon Park): Noted that previous postdeploy runners caused noisy alerts for minor spike in load times; recommended adding smoothing and an option to treat 'warning' vs 'fail'. We'll implement a two-tier result (PASS/WARN/FAIL) but keep pipeline-blocking only for FAIL. Adding to scope.

2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel: Updated orchestrator to accept 'strict' flag; default is strict=true for gate runs invoked by deploy pipeline. Agent now posts structured JSON to s3://redwood-postdeploy-results/<deploy-id>. Next: hook into Console dashboard ingestion.
